content:
The Digital Village

The world has truly become a global village, but the village square is now digital. Social media platforms have revolutionized how humans communicate, dismantling geographical barriers that once isolated communities. A teenager in Lagos can now share cultural trends with a peer in Tokyo instantly. However, this connectivity comes at a price. The constant barrage of curated lives fosters a sense of inadequacy among users, leading to mental health crises. Furthermore, the spread of misinformation travels faster than truth, often inciting violence or panic before facts can be verified. While the digital village offers boundless opportunities for networking and education, it lacks the accountability of the traditional village square, where anonymity was impossible.

questions.q: A suitable title for this passage is:
opts: The Pros and Cons of the Digital Age

questions.q: The phrase 'barrage of curated lives' implies:
opts: A heavy flow of edited and fake realities

questions.q: According to the passage, one negative effect of social media is:
opts: Mental health issues due to inadequacy

questions.q: The writer compares the 'digital village' to the 'traditional village' to highlight:
opts: The lack of accountability in the digital version

content:
The Dying Art of Conversation

In the past, evenings were spent on verandas, swapping stories under the moonlight. Today, the glow of smartphone screens has replaced the moonlight. Silence in a room full of people is no longer awkward; it is the norm, as everyone is engrossed in a private digital world. Psychologists warn that we are losing the art of conversation—the ability to read non-verbal cues, to listen with empathy, and to articulate thoughts without the safety net of an edit button. We are more connected than ever, yet we are increasingly lonely. The depth of human connection is being sacrificed for the breadth of digital connections.

opts: We have phones but no light
